problem: The three-contact, six-message count assumes the resolver already has the address of each name server, usually from glue records. If the NS target is out-of-bailiwick and no glue is supplied, the resolver must resolve the NS name first and the count rises.
fix: State the assumption: 'assuming glue records supply the name-server addresses, or those addresses are already cached'.

problem: 'That is three server contacts and six messages' can be misread as the total DNS messages including the host-to-resolver query and reply; the six count is only resolver-to-name-server messages.
fix: Say: 'That is three name-server contacts and six resolver-to-name-server messages; the host-resolver query and reply are additional'.

problem: Lowering TTL to 60 s only gives 60 s expiry after the IP change if the TTL was lowered at least one old TTL (86400 s) in advance. Caches that already stored the old 86400 s TTL keep it until it expires.
fix: Add the condition: lower the TTL at least 86400 s before the change, so caches refresh with the short TTL; then old records expire within 60 s after the change.

problem: The figure note '13 root servers' can be read as 13 physical machines, while the exam trap correctly says these are 13 named server identities served by many anycast copies.
fix: Change the note to '13 root server identities' or '13 root server names (anycast)'.
